name: Fort Steilacoom
blurb: The grounds of the 1849 US Army post, later Western State Hospital, in Lakewood. Old field boundaries, terraces and tracks survive under the grass.
about: The US Army built Fort Steilacoom in 1849 on Nisqually land, on a farm the Hudson's Bay Company had been running, after a clash at nearby Fort Nisqually that spring. It was the Army's headquarters in the Puget Sound War of 1855-56, and the Nisqually leader Leschi was hanged nearby in 1858; a historical court cleared his name in 2004. In 1871 the old post became the territory's asylum, today's Western State Hospital. Four of the officers' cottages still stand as a small museum, and much of the open ground around them is Fort Steilacoom Park.
